zh: 三个位置必须连续，而且每个值都要严格大于 threshold，等于阈值不算。只要知道以当前位置结尾、连续合格的元素有多少个，就能判断当前位置是否刚好凑满一个合格三元组。
从左到右扫描一遍，维护以当前位置结尾的连续合格计数，遇到不合格的值立即清零。计数第一次达到 3 时，这个三元组的起点就是最早的答案，可以直接结束。
读入 n、threshold 和数组，计数 streak 初始为 0；对下标 i，值大于 threshold 时 streak 加 1，否则 streak 归零；streak 一旦等于 3 就输出 i−2 并结束；扫描完仍未达到 3 则输出 −1。
en: The three positions must be consecutive and every value must be strictly greater than threshold; a value equal to the threshold does not count. If you know how many qualifying elements end consecutively at the current position, you can tell whether the current position completes a qualifying triple.

Scan once from left to right and keep the length of the run of qualifying elements ending at the current position, resetting it to zero at any failing value. The first time the run reaches 3, the start of that triple is the earliest answer and you can stop.

Read n, threshold and the array, and start with streak = 0. For index i, add 1 to streak if the value is greater than threshold, otherwise reset streak to 0. As soon as streak equals 3, print i - 2 and stop. If the scan ends without reaching 3, print -1.

explanationEn:
## Fixed source and the range from the same problem at another company

fastprep/Trade Desk/tdesk-buddies-greater-than-threshold.md at the fixed commit e66f809f4c953bce129f68491726176615db6afc explicitly asks for the first index i such that the three consecutive values numbers[i], numbers[i+1] and numbers[i+2] are all strictly greater than threshold, returning −1 if there is none. The original example [0,1,4,3,2,5] with threshold=1 and output 2 is correct. For i=1 the original explanation says only 4 exceeds 1, overlooking 3; the correct reason is that the 1 in the triple [1,4,3] is not strictly greater than 1, so the triple still fails. The original input and output are not modified.

The Constraints section of the TradeDesk raw text is none, so it has no numeric ranges. This problem explicitly adopts the ranges of the identical problem in the TikTok OCR, without claiming that the TradeDesk text carries them: OA LIST/TikTok_OA_(new CodeSignal version)/060_QQ_1755908365513.txt agrees with the raw text on the task, the earliest start, the strict comparison, −1 when there is no answer, the complete input [0,1,4,3,2,5] with threshold=1 and output 2, and the window-by-window explanation; 061_image.txt supplies 3≤n≤1000, −1000≤numbers[i]≤1000 and −1000≤threshold≤1000. This source link rests on the complete rules and example, not merely on a similar title.

The first public example keeps the TradeDesk original. The second, [-9,95,94,4,5] with threshold=42 and output −1, comes from OCR060 of the same problem; its source is marked explicitly and it is not presented as a TradeDesk example. The third, [−999,−999,−999] with threshold=−1000 and output 0, is added by this site. This site serializes the input as n threshold followed by the n array values, and outputs the 0-based start. No upstream code was executed.

## Approach

Scan from left to right and maintain streak, the number of consecutive elements ending at the current position that are strictly greater than threshold. If the current value qualifies, add 1; otherwise reset it to 0. When streak first reaches 3, return the current position minus 2; if it has not reached 3 by the end of the scan, return −1. Greater than or equal does not satisfy the rule, and the count must be reset at a failing value; scattered qualifying elements must not be accumulated.

## Proof of correctness

Maintain an invariant by induction: after processing index j, streak is exactly the length of the longest all-qualifying contiguous suffix ending at j. It holds initially for the empty prefix. When the current value qualifies, the old suffix is extended by 1; when it does not, there is no non-empty qualifying suffix, so it is reset to 0. Hence the invariant always holds.

The triple ending at j qualifies entirely if and only if streak is at least 3. When it first reaches 3, j−2 is a valid start, and no position ending earlier formed three in a row, so there is no earlier valid start. Returning immediately gives the smallest start. If it never reaches 3, every consecutive triple fails and returning −1 is correct.

## Complexity and edge cases

The scan takes O(n) time and O(1) extra space for the algorithm; reading the input needs O(n) space. The full n≤1000 is handled directly. Valid outputs are −1 or 0..n−3, and a match at the very end must be able to return n−3. With threshold=1000 no valid input has a solution; with threshold=−1000 a value equal to −1000 still does not qualify. When 4 or more consecutive elements qualify, return the earliest position, not the last triple.

## Independent verification

The oracle explicitly enumerates every window of length 3, checks for each one whether its minimum is strictly greater than threshold, and takes the smallest qualifying start; it does not use the consecutive-count recurrence. 163 unique inputs were run through the real reference subprocess. In addition, all 9801 combinations of n=3..7, values in {−1,0,1} and three thresholds were enumerated exhaustively, comparing the original reference with the window oracle.

The official cases include the full n=1000, the positive and negative extremes of the threshold and the array values, the first and the last triple, multiple matches, long qualifying runs, values exactly equal to the threshold, three qualifying values that are not consecutive, runs of two qualifying values that are always broken, and fixed-seed random data. Two negative controls, one that writes > as ≥ and one that returns the last match instead of the earliest, count as killed only after they exit normally on all official data.
